paragraphs.source_en: Proponents of a “soft” occupation focus on routine transactions and negative archaeology, while failing to consider the impact, both immediate and long-​term, of the mass slaughters with which the occupa- tion began, the widespread anxiety and terror, “countless captives,” enslavement and mass deportation to Mesopotamia, waves of panicked and indigent refugees fleeing west, the presence of a foreign army and its loathed religion, arbitrary op- pression and exactions by the occupation authorities, and onerous taxation that was used to fund an ongoing war against other Christians. Apart from all that, yes, life carried on as usual.39 Hundreds of thousands of Roman captives were deported to Mesopotamia or farther east. The lords of Iran were always in need of agricultural labor and skilled craftsmen, and had deported it from Romanía when they captured Antioch in 540 and Apameia in 573.
